events.title: October Revolution in Russia
events.description: On November 7, 1917 (October 25 in the Old Style Julian calendar), Bolshevik forces led by Vladimir Lenin stormed the Winter Palace in Petrograd and overthrew the Russian Provisional Government.
events.significance: It led to the establishment of the world's first communist state, which became the Soviet Union in 1922, and shaped global politics, ideology, and conflict throughout the 20th century.

events.title: Birth of Marie Curie
events.description: Maria Skłodowska, later known as Marie Curie, was born in Warsaw, then part of the Russian Empire. She became a pioneering physicist and chemist who researched radioactivity.
events.significance: Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different scientific fields (Physics in 1903 and Chemistry in 1911), and her work laid the foundation for modern nuclear physics and cancer treatment.

events.title: Collapse of the Tacoma Narrows Bridge
events.description: The first Tacoma Narrows Bridge in Washington State collapsed in a moderate wind just four months after opening, due to aeroelastic flutter that caused violent twisting oscillations.
events.significance: The failure, captured on film, became a landmark case study in engineering, leading to major changes in suspension bridge design and the development of aerodynamic testing for large structures.

events.title: Jeannette Rankin Elected to U.S. Congress
events.description: Jeannette Rankin of Montana was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives, becoming the first woman elected to national office in the United States, even before women's suffrage was guaranteed nationwide.
events.significance: Her election was a milestone for women's political representation in the United States and paved the way for future generations of female lawmakers.

events.title: David Dinkins Elected Mayor of New York City
events.description: David Dinkins won the New York City mayoral election, defeating Rudolph Giuliani in a close race and becoming the city's first African American mayor.
events.significance: His victory marked a historic breakthrough for Black political representation in one of America's largest and most influential cities.
